region_scene_page.compact: The late-1960s heavy guitar road where blues-rock, psychedelia, distortion, and extended soloing push toward hard rock and metal.
region_scene_page.standard: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory. The sound can be riff-heavy, organ-haunted, feedback-soaked, or jam-driven, but it usually keeps a blues pulse under the psychedelic surface. Compared with psychedelic pop, it is less cute and less compact. Compared with hard rock, it is more exploratory and acid-colored.
